name: Yao (Chiyao)
notes: Yao (Chiyao/Ciyao, Guthrie P.21), Bantu language spoken across southern Malawi, northern Mozambique and southern Tanzania. Standard (Malawian) orthography: five vowel qualities a/ɛ/i/ɔ/u with a length contrast optionally marked with a macron since plain vowel letters do not distinguish length. Voiceless plosives are aspirated (t → [tʰ]) while voiced ones are not. ⟨s⟩ is realised as retroflex [ʂ]. ⟨ŵ⟩ (w with circumflex) is the labiodental approximant /ʋ/, distinct from plain ⟨w⟩ /w/ — the same letter convention Nyanja uses. ⟨ly⟩ /ʎ/ and ⟨ny⟩ /ɲ/ are palatal digraphs; ⟨dy⟩ and ⟨j⟩ both spell /dʒ/. ⟨ng'⟩ marks the bare velar nasal /ŋ/, contrasting with a prenasalized velar stop sequence. Tone is phonologically and morphologically significant, as in other Bantu languages, but is not marked in the standard orthography.

sources.author: Ngunga, Armindo
sources.title: Phonology and Morphology of the Ciyao Verb
sources.notes: Descriptive phonology and morphology of Ciyao (Yao). Published as CSLI monograph (2000); the 1997 UC Berkeley dissertation version ('Lexical Phonology and Morphology and the Ciyao Verb System') is freely available at the given URL.

ancestors.notes: Yao branch of Bantu (Guthrie P.20), within Atlantic-Congo.

location.notes: Approximate centre of the Yao-speaking area, southern Malawi / Lake Malawi region.
